title: Use labels to organise issues
summary: Labels mark kinds of work so issues can be filtered or grouped. A label should have a meaning the team understands.
introduction: Labels mark kinds of work so issues can be filtered or grouped. A label should have a meaning the team understands. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain use labels to organise issues
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Labels mark kinds of work so issues can be filtered or grouped. A label should have a meaning the team understands.

blocks.code:
Issue: Search misses lowercase titles
Labels: bug, search
Meaning of bug: current behaviour differs from the intended behaviour
blocks.title: Use labels to organise issues

blocks.text: The labels help find related issues. They describe the work; they do not fix the problem or decide its priority by themselves.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose a label for adding beginner help text.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Too many overlapping labels can make a board harder to read.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
